claims.text: No unicode box-drawing, no fancy glyphs: only ``+ - |`` so it prints on a raw Windows console.
claims.why: The code uses only '+', '-', and '|' characters in _rule, _row, and _table.

claims.text: "hand_reachable" recall is partly self-graded and MUST NOT be blended with independently-derived recall into one headline number.
claims.why: _PROVENANCE_NOTE['hand_reachable'] explicitly states it is partially self-graded and should be treated as an upper bound, not blended.

claims.text: Errored rows carry no recall/compression/slice_tokens/... at all -- they get their own ERRORED section below, not a row in this recall/compression table.
claims.why: The comment describes behavior of code not in this chunk (the ERRORED section and harness._task_error_row).

claims.text: FOCUS-WITHHELD rows are excluded the same way, into their own section below.
claims.why: The loop in render_tier1 skips tasks with 'focus_withheld' key (t.get('focus_withheld')), and _focus_withheld_lines function is defined to generate a separate section.

claims.text: Absent (result.get) for any hand-built result dict that predates this field, and adds no lines when there are none.
claims.why: The function uses result.get('focus_withheld_ids') and returns empty list if falsy.

claims.text: Always shows both tiers (even when empty) and always prints the honesty note -- this block is the deliverable of this sprint.
claims.why: The function always prints 'PROVENANCE BREAKDOWN' header and iterates over 'primary' and 'quarantine' tiers, even if n_tasks==0 (it skips adding rows but still prints header). The honesty note is printed via _PROVENANCE_NOTE calls.
